rationale: While Popov et al. (2019) demonstrated that specific gain-of-function variants in YWHAZ (such as p.Ser230Trp) activate the RAF-ERK pathway and manifest with cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC)-like syndromic features, subsequent clinical reports and genomic databases (such as Wan et al. 2023 and GeneCards) establish that YWHAZ mutations also cause non-syndromic intellectual disability and developmental delay without CFC craniofacial or ectodermal abnormalities. Furthermore, the available literature records do not provide granular cohort-wide phenotypic numerators and denominators demonstrating that ectodermal and dysmorphic features exceed 50% across all primary YWHAZ cohorts.

evidence.text: Popov et al. identified novel variants in YWHAZ in individuals presenting with phenotypes consistent with cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC) syndrome and demonstrated that the S230W variant functions as a gain-of-function mutation activating the RAS-ERK pathway.

source.title: A YWHAZ Variant Associated With Cardiofaciocutaneous ...
source.quote: We recently identified novel variants in YWHAZ, a 14-3-3 family member, in individuals with a phenotype consistent with CFC that may potentially be deleterious and disease-causing.

evidence.text: Wan et al. identified a novel loss-of-function missense variant (p.Lys49Asn) in YWHAZ across a large three-generation family characterized by intellectual disability and global developmental delay rather than a syndromic CFC-like presentation.

source.title: YWHAZ variation causes intellectual disability and global ...
source.quote: To investigate the role of YWHAZ gene in intellectual disability and global developmental delay, we conducted whole-exon sequencing in all of the available members from a large three-generation family and we discovered that a novel variant of the YWHAZ gene was associated with intellectual disability and global developmental delay.

evidence.text: GeneCards curates YWHAZ as being causally implicated in both Popov-Chang Syndrome and Autosomal Dominant Non-Syndromic Intellectual Disability, demonstrating phenotypic heterogeneity beyond syndromic CFC phenotypes.

source.title: YWHAZ Gene
source.quote: Diseases associated with YWHAZ include Popov-Chang Syndrome and Autosomal Dominant Non-Syndromic Intellectual Disability.

conflicts: Popov et al. (2019) report that YWHAZ variants cause a cardiofaciocutaneous-like RASopathy via gain-of-function RAF-ERK activation, whereas Wan et al. (2023) report YWHAZ loss-of-function variants presenting primarily with non-syndromic intellectual disability and cognitive delay without typical CFC ectodermal or dysmorphic features.
Exact cohort phenotypic penetrance (e.g., whether >=50% display ectodermal involvement) is not uniformly supported across broader YWHAZ-associated neurodevelopmental cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Does variant mechanism (gain-of-function vs. loss-of-function in YWHAZ) strictly delineate CFC-like syndromic RASopathy from non-syndromic neurodevelopmental delay?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the genotype-phenotype correlation between RAS-ERK activating mutations (e.g., p.Ser230Trp) and loss-of-function alleles (e.g., p.Lys49Asn) will establish whether Popov-Chang syndrome represents a distinct allelic disorder or part of a broad continuum.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true clinical sensitivity of specific HPO terms (hypertelorism, sparse hair, keratosis pilaris) across an international aggregated cohort of all published YWHAZ cases?
new_directions.rationale: A systematic international multi-center registry analysis is required to determine exact numerators and denominators for ectodermal and dysmorphic features to guide differential diagnosis from other DEE and neurodevelopmental conditions.
